command:
set -eo pipefail
cd /tmp
echo "== verify staged inputs against their pinned sha256 =="
printf '%s  %s\n' c753ba28b98b750659e27a7f9e0ceb224e26a5c767ce676a219c0a20adae5259 ensembl116_pep_one_per_gene.fa.gz > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256

# The family comes from hmmsearch's own tblout, so this recipe aligns what hmmer FOUND
# rather than a set someone curated by hand: 7tm_1 (PF00001, class A GPCRs) is the largest
# family in the human one-protein-per-gene set at 906 members. awk and gzip are base-image
# utilities, not a second scientific tool -- this is still one tool, one task.
gzip -dc hits.tbl.gz | grep -v '^#' | awk '$3=="7tm_1"{print $1}' | sort -u > ids.txt
WANT=$(awk 'END{print NR}' ids.txt)
# Ensembl pep sequences carry `*` for stop codons -- 111 of them across 23 of these 906
# proteins, from readthrough and annotation artefacts. `*` is not an amino acid, and MAFFT
# silently drops it (measured: every other character count is preserved exactly). Stripping
# it HERE rather than accounting for it later is what keeps the cross-check honest: muscle
# need not handle `*` the same way mafft does, and a divergence from stop codons would be a
# difference in input handling masquerading as a difference in alignment.
gzip -dc ensembl116_pep_one_per_gene.fa.gz | awk '
  NR==FNR {want[$1]=1; next}
  /^>/ {id=substr($1,2); keep=(id in want); if (keep) print; next}
  keep {gsub(/\*/,""); print}
' ids.txt - > family.fa
GOT=$(grep -c '^>' family.fa)
INRES=$(awk '!/^>/{n+=length($0)} END{printf "%.0f", n}' family.fa)
echo "family 7tm_1: want $WANT ids, extracted $GOT sequences, $INRES residues"

echo "== mafft --auto, 906 GPCR sequences =="
# --thread is pinned: mafft's progressive alignment is deterministic for a fixed thread
# count, and an unpinned count is the subtlest way an exact assertion goes flaky.
T0=$(date +%s)
mafft --auto --thread 8 family.fa > aln.fa 2> mafft.log
T1=$(date +%s); WALL=$(( T1 - T0 ))
# mafft prints "Strategy:" and names the strategy on the FOLLOWING line.
STRATEGY=$(awk '/^Strategy:/{getline; print $1; exit}' mafft.log)

# An alignment must not alter sequence CONTENT -- only insert gaps. So the ungapped residue
# count is a conservation identity: exact, thread-independent, and it catches the failure that
# actually happens (a sequence silently dropped or truncated) which any score band would pass.
SEQS=$(grep -c '^>' aln.fa)
RES=$(awk '!/^>/{gsub(/-/,""); n+=length($0)} END{printf "%.0f", n}' aln.fa)
# Every row of an alignment is the same length, by definition of being an alignment.
read -r LMIN LMAX <<<"$(awk '/^>/{if(l!=""){if(l<mn||mn=="")mn=l; if(l>mx)mx=l}; l=0; next}
  {l+=length($0)} END{if(l<mn)mn=l; if(l>mx)mx=l; print mn, mx}' aln.fa)"

{
  echo "family               7tm_1 (PF00001), from hmmsearch's own tblout"
  echo "ids_from_hmmer       $WANT   want exactly 906"
  echo "sequences_extracted  $GOT   want == ids_from_hmmer"
  echo "input_residues       $INRES   want exactly 311969 (stop codons stripped)"
  echo "aligned_sequences    $SEQS   want == sequences_extracted"
  echo "aligned_residues     $RES   want exactly 311969   [CONSERVATION: gaps only, no edits]"
  echo "row_length           $LMIN..$LMAX   want exactly 4340   [reproducible: 2 runs, identical]"
  echo "mafft_strategy       $STRATEGY   (observation)"
  echo "wall_s               $WALL"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt
test "$WANT" -eq 906
test "$GOT"  -eq "$WANT"
test "$INRES" = '311969'
test "$SEQS" -eq "$GOT"
test "$RES"  = '311969'
test "$LMIN" -eq "$LMAX"
# MEASURED, twice, on identical bytes with --thread pinned: mafft returns 4340 columns both
# times, so the alignment length is exact-or-wrong here. muscle is NOT like this (5633 then
# 5636 on the same input), which is why only this recipe asserts its column count.
test "$LMIN" -eq 4340
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
